description: AI-native OS where the AI is a first-class user — not a chatbot bolted on top.

summary.one_liner: SomaOS is an experimental Linux-based operating system with a custom DRM/KMS compositor and an LLM agent that acts as a peer desktop user alongside the human.
summary.what_it_does: The project builds a minimal bootable Linux image (via Buildroot) that boots into a custom Rust compositor rendering directly to DRM/KMS framebuffers, with no X11 or Wayland server. The desktop has floating windows, a dock, a menu bar, and an AI sidebar with chat, plan cards, and a human-approval (HITL) modal. A Rust agent daemon exposes roughly 40 built-in capability actions across filesystem, process, system, network, package, browser, vision, meta, and desktop-control modules, plus user-defined shell-backed capabilities loaded from JSON files. The agent can drive the desktop (open/focus windows, type text) and spawn declarative widget-tree windows at runtime. It supports Ollama, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini providers via native tool calling, and records desktop events for workflow learning unless private mode is on. The README describes the project as v2.0 with a "soma-substrate" crate for resource-state monitoring and action tiers, and it lists dual-interface apps (soma-sheets, soma-docs) as planned or partially implemented.
use_cases: experimenting with an AI-native desktop environment
running a local LLM agent that controls apps and windows
building a custom DRM/KMS compositor in Rust
giving an AI agent human-approved access to system commands
prototyping self-extending agent capabilities via JSON definitions
booting a minimal Linux image in a VM with an AI desktop
notable: Human and AI agent share the same desktop; the agent uses structured IPC rather than pixel-scraping
Compositor renders directly to DRM/KMS with no X11 or Wayland server
Agent can propose new capabilities as JSON shell templates, which the human approves through a HITL gate
Private mode disables desktop event observation for workflow learning
Native tool calling across multiple LLM providers with a keyword fast-path layer
caveats: Dev mode uses a winit window and skips the login screen; the full bare-metal path needs a Buildroot image or VM
Requires Ollama and a local model (default qwen2.5-coder:7b) for the default configuration
Several described features, such as the WebKitGTK browser embedding and soma-sheets/soma-docs AgentAPI, are presented as future or long-term stack items
Image builds depend on Docker, and VM setup guides are separate per architecture (x86_64 and ARM64)
keywords: let an ai run commands on my computer
build my own os in rust
